messages:
ria: Quick sync — thinking about a safer hotstart path for mixed safetensors + gzipped shards. Current problem: large models with many tiny shards cause warmup thrash under load. We need a coordination scheme for backpressure + prioritized hydration.

matt: I hit this in staging. Too many concurrent prefetches = IO queue blows and GPU sits idle. We need a way to limit inflight chunk fetches per-host and per-request.

li: +1. Also some shards are already cached at edge, others stream from S3. Can we express priority hints in the manifest? e.g., "hot": true for first-n shards.

ria: Precisely. Proposal: augment manifest with three optional fields: priority_hint (int), compress ("gz"/"none"), and estimated_uncompressed_bytes. Priority_hint drives early hydrating; lower numbers = higher priority.

sam: What about evictions? If we OOM during warmup, we should abort low-priority prefetches and keep the high-priority ones. Need clear abort semantics.

nina: Also consider streaming decode for gzipped tensors to avoid full decompress before device copy. That helps memory pressure.

ria: Example manifest snippet I sketched:

```
{\n  "shards": [\n    {"path": "model-0000.safetensors.gz", "priority_hint": 0, "compress": "gz", "range": [0, 1048576]},\n    {"path": "model-0001.safetensors.gz", "priority_hint": 1, "compress": "gz", "range": [0, 2048576]}\n  ],\n  "hotstart_strategy": "priority-first",\n  "prefetch_budget_bytes": 134217728\n}
```

matt: That looks good. Implementation Q: is priority per-shard or per-layer? Per-shard is simpler for the loader. We can extend later for layer-level markings.

li: We should also expose a per-deployment prefetch_budget override via config so Dedicated customers can tune for their infra.

sam: For backpressure, propose token-bucket style inflight_fetch_slots with two dimensions: global per-host and per-request window. That prevents a single request from monopolizing IO during a big prefix.

nina: If we abort lower-priority fetches mid-decompress, we need a safe cancellation path in the decompressor so we don't leak buffers. Warmup-bot: queued job metrics should account for cancellations.

warmup-bot: FYI — existing warmup queue already tracks attempts and failures (metric: warmup.fetch_attempts). No cancellation hook today.

ria: Good to know. So plan: 1) schema bump for manifest (priority_hint, compress, estimated_uncompressed_bytes), 2) loader implements inflight slots + per-request cap, 3) cancellation API in decompressor, 4) metrics for cancelled_prefetches and prefetch_latency_by_priority.

matt: One more: graceful degrade policy — if the high-priority shards aren't available within X ms, fallback to a smaller but compatible model variant (e.g., 8-bit quantized). That should be a routing-level decision we can express in the manifest as fallback_model_tag.

li: For hosted API, we can set reasonable defaults for prefetch_budget and inflight slots; Dedicated customers can override. Add an opt-in for streaming-decompress to avoid extra temporary storage.

sam: Tests: unit test for slot throttling, integration test that simulates S3 tail latency + eviction during warmup. Need perf harness to validate we actually reduce GPU idle time.

nina: Security: ensure compressed shards are verified (checksum) before streaming into decompressor. Don't trust client-provided sizes.

ria: Agreed. Add checksum and signature fields in manifest. Also need clear migration story: loader should ignore unknown fields and default to previous behavior (backwards compatibility).

matt: Can someone file a slim RFC PR? I can help write the prefetch-slot logic but prefer the schema to be settled first.

ria: I'll open a draft RFC with the manifest diff and the operator config knobs. Link when ready — want review from eng-runtime and eng-sre.

li: Ping me on the PR. I can sketch Dedicated defaults and security checks.

warmup-bot: Note scheduled: warmup-queue-alert rule will be updated if we add cancelled_prefetches metric.

sam: Thanks — can we land a short POC (loader + fake gz stream) in a week? If so, we can test on smaller models first.

ria: Yes. POC plan: loader changes (throttling + priorities), decompressor cancellation API, manifest parser bump. Keep default behavior identical unless manifest hint present.

nina: I'll own the tests for streaming-decompress correctness and memory-safety.

matt: Sounds good. One last nit — naming: call the feature "priority hotstart" or "hydration hints"? I prefer hydration hints.

ria: Hydration hints it is. I'll use that in the RFC. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
